questions.scenario: A developer fixes a typo in `V3__add_account_daily_limit.sql`, which already ran in UAT and production. The next deployment fails with a Flyway checksum mismatch.
questions.question: What is the correct approach?
options: Revert the edit to V3 and put the correction in a new migration V6
questions.explanation: Applied migrations are immutable history. Corrections go in new migrations so every environment converges the same way. Clean would drop production data.

questions.scenario: Your team needs to rename `account.number` to `account.nuban` while the service runs as several instances with rolling deploys.
questions.question: Which approach avoids breaking old instances during the deploy?
options: Expand and contract: add nuban, write both, backfill, switch reads, then later drop number
Take the database offline over the weekend
ALTER TABLE account RENAME COLUMN number TO nuban in one release
questions.explanation: During a rolling deploy, old code still reads number. Spreading the change over several backward-compatible releases keeps every running version working.

questions.scenario: A Flyway migration `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_txn_ref ON txn(reference);` fails with 'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block'.
questions.question: How do you fix it?
options: Put it in its own migration and configure that script not to run in a transaction (executeInTransaction=false)
questions.explanation: Flyway wraps each migration in a transaction by default, which CONCURRENTLY forbids. Removing CONCURRENTLY would block writes on a hot table during the build.

questions.scenario: You need a reporting view that the analytics team changes often. You want it recreated whenever its definition changes.
questions.question: Which Flyway migration type fits?
options: A repeatable migration R__view_name.sql with CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
A new versioned migration V__ for every change
questions.explanation: Repeatable migrations re-run when their checksum changes, after all versioned migrations, which is ideal for views, functions and stored procedures.

questions.scenario: The team is adopting Flyway on a 10-year-old production database that already has 140 tables and no migration history.
questions.question: Which Flyway feature lets it start tracking from the current state?
options: baseline (e.g. baseline version 1, with new changes as V2 onwards)
questions.explanation: Baseline records the existing schema as a known version so Flyway only applies migrations newer than it.

questions.scenario: A migration adding a column needs an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on `account`, but a long-running report holds a conflicting lock. All payment queries queue up behind the waiting migration and the app freezes.
questions.question: What precaution limits the damage?
options: SET lock_timeout (e.g. '5s') at the start of the migration so it fails fast instead of queueing traffic behind it, then retry later
questions.explanation: Lock requests queue in order; a waiting DDL lock blocks later queries too. A short lock_timeout makes the migration give up quickly, keeping production responsive.

questions.scenario: A bank's platform team standardised on Liquibase. You need to explain to a Flyway user how Liquibase identifies a change it has already applied.
questions.question: Which answer is correct?
options: By the timestamp of the deploy
By the changeset's id plus author plus changelog file path, recorded in DATABASECHANGELOG
questions.explanation: Liquibase tracks changesets by id/author/file and stores checksums in DATABASECHANGELOG, whereas Flyway uses the version in the file name and flyway_schema_history.
